title: Negotiated desktop bridge admission and replay lifetime

node.description: Present only while the polling node waits for the owner's confirmation; commands is then empty.

deadline_enforced.description: True only for an explicit pickup TTL. Missing means legacy enforced expiry; false uses expires_at only for acknowledged replay-record retirement.

home_tiers.description: The Home ceiling for this node (contracts/device_routing_v1.schema.json $defs/Tiers). The node runs a non-read command only when its tier is true here AND in its own switch; absent means a Home that predates ceilings.

boot_id.description: Fresh per node process; the Home refuses an earlier boot of a node ID that polls again after a newer boot (contracts/desktop_node_registry_v1.schema.json x-identity.boot).

rtt_ms.description: Round trip of the node's latest exchange that the Home answered without a hold (a poll carrying results or stream frames).

SystemFacts.description: Optional agent-reported OS, architecture and command shells so the model writes commands for the device's own shell. Agents without it stay admissible; a server stores only these declared fields and drops a malformed object.

x-semantics.negotiation: Agent advertises protocol_version=3. Missing version selects legacy v2; explicit unsupported versions fail with 426 before registration or acknowledgement. Once v3 is observed, the agent refuses downgrade within that connection run.
x-semantics.expiry: Default commands have no pickup deadline. deadline_enforced=false makes expires_at a stable replay-retention horizon starting at first dispatch; completion and all output ACKs are required before retirement. Explicit TTLs retain creation-based enforced pickup expiry. Missing deadline_enforced preserves legacy server semantics.
x-semantics.replay: Keep running and unacknowledged IDs. Reclaim only expired finite-deadline IDs after completion and acknowledgement. Legacy IDs remain pinned until restart without changing legacy demand-driven admission. In-memory deduplication is process-local; a command whose tier is not read/control is also journaled durably by the node (lib/desktop_agent/_journal.py), so a repeated command id is answered from the journal and never re-run, also after a node restart. A command id the device routing produces is the tool call's idempotency key.
x-semantics.flow_control: Agent reports execution_slots on every poll. Server delivers no more normal work than those slots, counting claimed nonterminal work; cancellation bypasses execution slots. Every response stays within command_batch. Resident outboxes scale independently; wire prefixes and per-frame limits retain the result/stream floors. Uploads with output acknowledge without long-poll delay, and the agent drains a remaining prefix immediately. Slots are resource-derived advisory server delivery credits; the agent does not reject already-issued work for a local worker quota. Memory overflow spools privately, preserving output until acknowledgement or joined shutdown.
x-semantics.authority: The authenticated server owner and device claim remain the settlement authority. The agent independently validates target_agent_id before acknowledging a batch or dispatching controls. Credentials never authorize a discovered route.
x-semantics.admission: Commands execute under actual demand. execution_slots is a compatibility poll-window hint, never a CPU/memory or replay-count admission permit. Bounded rotating active-ID pages acknowledge delivery; the server retains owner/device-bound acknowledgements until settlement, so omitted IDs cannot block later jobs.
